elements.element: No MFN (most-favoured-nation) obligation imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall not be required to offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier."

elements.element: MFN pricing running in Customer's favour is permitted / not prohibited
elements.evidence: No language restricts Customer from receiving favourable terms; 12.3 preserved: "Nothing restricts Customer from ... engaging any supplier"

elements.element: Any MFN obligation limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: No product limitation appears; clause instead negates the obligation entirely
No duration stated in 7.2 as revised
No comparison carve-outs present in 7.2 or 12.3

reasons: The single operator flip ("shall not be required to offer") eliminates the Customer-side MFN in 7.2, achieving the locked preferred position with no MFN burden on Customer.
Fallback elements (defined product, 12-month term, comparison carve-outs) are absent, but that is irrelevant since the preferred level is fully met and the two levels are separate bargains.
Change is confined to a short phrase within one sentence; no whole-clause rewrite, new exception, or boilerplate added.
Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no most-favoured-customer commitment is untouched and now consistent rather than contradictory; no undefined terms or dangling mechanics introduced.

Drafting note only: the resulting double negative ("shall not be required to offer ... no less favourable") reads awkwardly; a cleaner deletion of the sentence would be equally minimal, but the operative effect is unambiguous.
